Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB186.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linyexi. Linye Tongqi owns the retained address: of old the old man Bodhidharma said — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; mind like a wall, and so one may enter the way. But as this mountain monk sees it, not so: inside, one must let out; outside, one must let in — like a pearl rolling in a bowl, and so one may enter the way. And did not the great master Linji say: one person spends kalpas on the road yet never leaves home; another leaves home yet is not on the road — which of these two deserves the offerings of gods and men? He came down from the seat. Assembly before me! want to know these two faces? He snatched up the staff and rapped it once: this too does not go outside this message — and tell me, what message is it? Two more raps: when the dragon gets water its spirit rises; when the tiger meets the mountain its power grows.

Old man Bodhidharma — please step outside the door; Deshan and Linji — called over to plant trees. Here heaven and earth lie clear and still, all things at peace: the root-knowing, the all-knowing, stream out from this place; the concentration gates and the power gates are gathered back in here as well. The men of old, once they had it, nurtured the holy embryo in thatch hut and stone room — fame and profit never touched their hearts, sights and sounds never snagged their thoughts. On what ground do they stand? — sky high, the array of forms upright; sea wide, a hundred rivers pay homage. Then he took up the sealed notice and said: inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — and if Hanshan and Shide come, what then? Soo-loo, soo-loo.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB345.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhuyan Yan of Suzhou. Zhu'an Zhenyan owns the retained enshrining address: the sage has no self, and so nothing is not himself; the body of reality has no form — who speaks of self and other? A circle drawn with the whisk: this is the treasury of the thus-come, the wondrous pure bright heart. Inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in. The myriad kinds have never shifted; the thousand sages stand straight as a bowstring — the two or three of the eastern earth, the four and seven of the western heaven. All told, no effort of words gets it down; only grasp the sun and moon inside the pot, and then you know the world beyond the measure — beyond the reach of the great eye, past the peering of Sakra.

Lingji Xingguan owns the retained echo-answer: a monk asked — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — what serves as the boundary? The master said: inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — I say there is nothing that can serve as the boundary. How then does one turn the body over? — that must be you yourself, sir. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB468.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shanyi Chun. Shanyi Ruchun owns the retained retreat-opening: hold the firm pass, sit across the forking roads — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; in this bright business there is plainly no consulting, and in ninety days it bends of itself. Bends to what, tell me? This mountain monk drew legs on the snake; you all hunt a rope to bind yourselves with — and even if you scatter from here, each of you already carries thirty smart blows under his heels. And yet the thing is not one-sided. Why? Old man Yama is reckoning the rice-money. Do not say the mountain monk said nothing — and what, then, did he say? A long silence, one rap of the staff: all alike they walk the road below the mountain — each pair of eyes reads its own wind and smoke. One shout; he came down.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB294.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liangting Ting of Yunxi. Liangting Jingting owns the retained solstice address: at the winter solstice the one yang is born, flowers open in a spring beyond the kalpa — he is used to cooking rice-less meals, wholly bent on tuning the string-less zither. Has it not been said: the wine of the dark has a thin taste, the greatest music has scarce sound; thunder lies in the earth in Return, and the former kings closed the passes at the solstice — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; merchants and travelers do not journey; to step out the gate is to step into grass — and even never stepping out, it is grass, grass, all the way. The queen does not inspect the regions: the golden hall towers, locked on the honored one — take care not to leave the palace and lose your station. Assembly! look — one pool of clear blue, cold reeds on both banks: the heart of heaven and earth stands forced into the open — and when the bronze dial paces the shadow and the reed pipe flies its ash, what is it good for?

Senses.Explanation: Inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — the double-sealed gate of the wall-instruction, spoken over retreats, statues, and solstices, and then flipped. Linye Tongqi, in the hall: of old the old man Bodhidharma said — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; mind like a wall, and so one may enter the way — but as this mountain monk sees it, not so: inside, one must let out; outside, one must let in; like a pearl rolling in a bowl, and so one may enter the way; and did not great master Linji say — one person spends kalpas on the road yet never leaves home, another leaves home yet is not on the road — which deserves the offerings of gods and men? the staff rapped: this too does not go outside this message. Sanyi Mingyu, sealing a monk's retreat: snap the staff, hang the bowl; old man Bodhidharma, please step outside; Deshan and Linji, come plant trees; the root-knowing streams out from here, the concentration gates gather back in; and the notice taken up: inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — and if Hanshan and Shide come, what then? soo-loo, soo-loo. Zhu'an Zhenyan, enshrining the two statues: the sage has no self and so nothing is not himself; the body of reality has no form — who speaks of self and other? a circle drawn with the whisk: the treasury of the thus-come, the wondrous pure bright heart — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; the myriad kinds have never shifted, the thousand sages stand bowstring-straight; only grasp the sun and moon inside the pot, and you will know the world beyond the measure. Lingji Xingguan, in the exchange: the monk asked — what serves as the boundary? and the master answered with the couplet itself — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in — I say there is nothing that can serve as the boundary; how does one turn the body over? that must be you yourself, sir; the monk shouted, the master struck. Shanyi Ruchun, opening the retreat: hold the firm pass, sit across the forking roads — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; in this bright business no consulting, and in ninety days it bends of itself; this mountain monk drew legs on the snake, you all hunt a rope to bind yourselves; even scattering from here, thirty smart blows already wait under each pair of heels — and old man Yama is reckoning the rice-money; one rap of the staff: all alike walk the road below the mountain, each pair of eyes reads its own wind and smoke. Liangting Jingting, at the solstice: the one yang is born, flowers open in a spring beyond the kalpa — used to cooking rice-less meals, wholly bent on the string-less zither; the wine of the dark has a thin taste, the greatest music scarce sound; thunder lies in the earth in Return, and the former kings closed the passes at the solstice — inside, do not let out; outside, do not let in; merchants and travelers do not journey; to step out the gate is grass, and never stepping out is still grass, grass, all the way — look: one pool of clear blue, cold reeds on both banks, the heart of heaven and earth forced into the open.
